text:
alex: Quick midday check-in: merged the routing-policy PR that adds per-route JWT checks and a new rate tier; pushed to staging at 11:02am. Link: https://git.redwood/rgw/pull/482
mira: Nice. Saw some 429s in the e2e job after the merge. I think the batching change bumped concurrent tokens for /api/v1/generate.
jamal: @mira I'll pick this up. Can you paste the failing test logs?
mira: Here — the auth handshake timeout then 429s.
sofia: FYI the auth key rotation script ran at 11:05 and rotated the staging KMS key. Could be a timing hole.
alex: Huh. Didn't think rotation would affect short-lived bearer checks — but maybe the cached public key wasn't refreshed. @jamal can you run a quick redeploy after clearing the auth cache?
jamal: On it. Also leaving a note: I'm going to canary a tweak to rate limits (increase burst for gen route). Will monitor latency.
deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-service v1.12.3 -> staging (canary: 10%)
jamal: Redeployed and cleared auth cache. Monitoring metrics — 429s dropped immediately.
mira: Awesome, looks stable now. I'll re-run the failing e2e job.
sofia: Suggestion: add an event when KMS rotation happens to trigger a cache refresh in routing-service.
alex: Agree. Filing a small follow-up: https://issues.redwood/PLAT-1982
mira: Blockers: none now. Today: finish the rollout plan doc and pair with @jamal on the rate tuning.
jamal: Today: watch canary, open PR for cache refresh hook, ping infra for longer retention on auth keys.
sofia: I'll add the KMS -> cache refresh proposal to the infra board. Also pinging @ops for FYI.
alex: Thanks all. If anyone sees regressions, ping #incidents and @oncall.

Code snippet we ran during debug:
```
routes:
  - id: /api/v1/generate
    auth: jwt
    rate_limit:
      steady: 60/min
      burst: 200
```
